statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope 2 in the x direction and slope 5 in the y direction.
(a) A change of 0.5 in x and 0.4 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=2 when x=3 and y=6, what is the value of z when x=2.9 and y=6.2?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope 2 in the x direction, and slope 5 in the y direction, we have: z = 2 x + 5 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (2 (x + \Delta x) + 5(y + \Delta y) + c) - (2 x + 5 y + c) = 2 \Delta x + 5 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = 0.5 and \Delta y = 0.4, we have \Delta z = 2 (0.5) + 5(0.4) = 3. So a 0.5 change in x and a 0.4 change in y produces a 3 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=2 when x=3 and y=6, the value of z when x=2.9 and y=6.2 will be z = 2 + \Delta z = 2 + 2\Delta x + 5\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 3 to 2.9 and y changes from 6 to 6.2. We have \Delta x = 2.9 - 3 = -0.1 and \Delta y = 6.2 - 6 = 0.2. Therefore, when x=2.9 and y=6.2, we have z = 2 + 2 \cdot(-0.1) + 5\cdot(0.2) = 2.8.
